subject: biology
title: Food Chains and Webs
welcome_lead: Follow energy as it flows from sunlight through plants and into hungry animals.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on food chains, food webs and energy transfer.
final_note: You now understand how energy flows through producers, consumers and decomposers.

concepts.def: Plant that makes its own food.
Animal that eats other living things.
Breaks down dead material to release nutrients.
Shows what eats what in a line.
Movement of energy through a food chain.

walkthroughs.body_html: A food chain starts with a producer. Arrows show energy flow. For example: grass → rabbit → fox. Each arrow means 'is eaten by'.
Most animals eat more than one type of food. A food web joins many chains so we can see the real connections in a habitat.
Decomposers like fungi and bacteria break down dead plants and animals. They return nutrients to the soil so producers can grow again.

options: Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.

mcqs.q: Why is negative feedback the default mechanism in homeostasis?
options: Negative feedback only operates when something goes wrong in the body.
It opposes deviations from a set point, returning the variable toward its normal value — keeping internal conditions stable.
Negative feedback amplifies changes to make them more noticeable.

mcqs.q: What does a gene code for?
options: Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.
Transcription happens in mitochondria where ATP is produced.
A gene codes for a specific physical feature like eye colour directly.
Typically a polypeptide (protein) — through transcription to mRNA and translation by ribosomes.
